Every agent-chat product is converging on the same architecture: an event-sourced store in front of a replaceable coding-CLI actor. This paper maps which wins are shared across every provider (build once, inherit forever), which are edgies (Claude and Codex need special treatment), and where Google, GLM, and Grok land — so we can steer feature priority by leverage instead of by provider.

The layer cake — where wins are shared and where they are not

The decisive structural fact, verified in t3code's source: their five shipped providers (Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode) plus four queued (GitHub Copilot, Gemini, “ACP Registry”, Pi Agent) all hang off one provider seam. Grok and Cursor are not even two adapters — they are one AcpSessionRuntime with thin per-vendor extension modules. The architecture sorts into three altitudes:

Everything in the top box is a compounding asset: the day a second runtime lands, PortableDoc replies, the sidebar, co-viewing, and Papers-from-plans work for it on day one. t3 renders markdown; nobody else renders replies as living documents that radiate to a TUI. That is ours regardless of provider.

Win-wins — the nine universal heuristics

These are the invariants t3code's contracts layer enforces on all five providers, and they map one-to-one onto what our Recorder/store already does. Features designed against these are provider-blind by construction.

1. Session = durable id + opaque resume cursor. Claude: --session-id/--resume. Codex: {threadId} with fallback-to-fresh on unknown thread. ACP: session/load. The cursor's shape is provider-private; the pattern is universal.
2. Turn lifecycle — started / streaming / settled / interrupted. Fold-on-settle, settle-gated ✓ glyphs, and “You stopped after 42s” are all defined on the lifecycle, never on the wire.
3. Our store owns display; the CLI owns model memory. Never tail provider disk state. Holds in every family.
4. Approvals = correlate by request id, answer allow/deny(+message), force-cancel all on teardown. Claude control_request, Codex JSON-RPC approval requests keyed by approvalId, ACP session/request_permission — same skeleton, three vocabularies.
5. Interrupt turn ≠ stop session as distinct verbs, everywhere.
6. Model/mode as an intent-vs-observed pair (our wave-5 model_choice vs observed fact) — generalizes untouched.
7. Usage and cost off the result frame. Every provider reports something; normalize to one headroom ring.
8. Auth is inherited from the host CLI's login, never implemented. Multi-account = home-directory overlay ($HOME for Claude; CODEX_HOME authOverlay with private auth.json symlinks for Codex). We already run this model on guerrilla.
9. Idle reaper + lazy resume, AI titles with a human-rename clobber guard, sticky drafts, two-phase honest send — all provider-blind.

Below the seam, cost should be paid at family granularity — one runtime per protocol, thin extensions per vendor. Never one bespoke build per provider.

Family A — stream-json NDJSON (we own this)
claude --print --input/output-format stream-json over stdio. No handshake; init arrives with the first turn. Members: Claude Code — and every Anthropic-compatible backend: GLM (z.ai), Kimi, MiniMax ride the SAME binary via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + token. Our existing Elixir Port covers all of them.
Family B — ACP JSON-RPC (the strategic bet)
Agent Client Protocol (Zed lineage). initialize handshake, session/load, session/request_permission, capability negotiation. Members: Gemini CLI, Grok, Cursor (agent acp), Qwen Code, plus t3's coming-soon “ACP Registry” = any ACP agent. One Elixir ACP runtime unlocks the whole set.
Family C — codex app-server (trigger-gated candidate for #2)
Persistent JSON-RPC server: initialize/initialized, thread/start, turn/start, turn/interrupt, thread/read, thread/rollback. Fine-grained item/* notifications (reasoning text deltas, patch updates). High value (t3code's DEFAULT driver, real thinking text, rollback un-cuts rewind) but 3,128 reference lines for ONE provider vs ACP's 988 for four — rev 4 gates it behind a demand trigger and a fresh Codex-vs-ACP re-score. See “Why Codex second — and why it waits”.
Family D — HTTP + SSE (the aggregator escape hatch)
OpenCode runs as a local HTTP server (@opencode-ai/sdk, event.subscribe SSE pump). One adapter = 75+ models including GLM, Qwen, and local/Ollama — long-tail coverage without chasing each vendor's CLI.

Five independent strategy agents (Claude-maximalist, transcendence architect, daily-driver, contrarian, horizon scout) reviewed this paper against the repo, the t3code source, and a live probe of the installed CLI. Claude-maximalist
The special is MCP loopback — Claude gets scoped hands over Barkpark itself (tasks, Papers, boards) because the chat and the CMS are the same BEAM app. No competitor has a product behind their chat. Plus workflow cockpit v2 and --fork-session branching.
Daily-driver
The transcript war is won; build the WORKDAY around sessions — needs-you inbox, notifications via the existing mail relay, FTS search over chat history, the epic's bp-task ledger live beside the rail, phone-answerable cards.
Horizon scout
The CLI itself (--bg, claude agents --json, --remote-control, --from-pr) proves the future: fleet dashboards, approval-from-phone, sessions as a searchable corpus. Our Recorder is already an agent host that happens to render chat.

Best-Claude-that-transcends is real: the portability tax on Claude UX is ≈zero — the tax lands on architecture (the verbatim-PubSub contract), and half of it is Claude robustness profit (init-as-turn-boundary, result-sniffing in the view). ACP is 988 reference lines for 4+ providers vs Codex 3,128 for one. And the top risk isn't provider strategy at all — it's undocumented wire frames under our moat feature.

(1) A wire-contract harness (fixture-replay per PR, nightly real-binary smoke, pinned CLI version with explicit upgrade step) precedes all seam work — the differentiator rides undocumented frames. (2) The seam's canonical-event refactor lands Claude-only and behavior-frozen first. (3) The Codex wave is trigger-gated: it starts only on real user demand or a dry Claude backlog, and at trigger time Codex vs ACP is re-scored with fresh data. (4) Standing roadmap rule: every wave carries at least one Barkpark-coupled item — the moat (PortableDoc replies, plans→Papers, the rail, MCP loopback, co-viewing, self-hosted trust) is the priority spine; generic chrome justifies itself against it. (5) GLM/Kimi instances ship only after a frame-survival probe passes as a HARD gate.

The focus pair remains Claude + Codex — these are the CLIs our users actually run. The engineering case for Codex as provider #2 still stands, for three reasons:

1. Codex is the seam's forcing function. You never trust an abstraction with one implementation. Claude and Codex are the two most different wires on the horizon — a no-handshake NDJSON pipe versus a persistent JSON-RPC server with initialize/initialized, threads, and server-side state. Depth with Claude proves the product; the seam is proven Claude-first; the second wire is bought on demand with fresh data. Everything above the seam compounds either way — and the capability matrix is the steering wheel.
